history.summary: Pallippurathukavu Bhagavathi Temple at Chandakadavu/Kodimatha, about 1 km south of Kottayam town, is a Devi (Durga/Bhagavathi) shrine noted for the traditional ritual art form Thiyyattu and the annual Kumbhakuta Mahotsavam held on Pathamudaya (10th day of the Malayalam month Medam), when the night ritual Garudan Thookkam draws large crowds. Note: do not confuse with the Neelamperoor Palli Bhagavathy Temple ~16 km south of Kottayam, a separate shrine famous for Padayani. No reliable source found for the temple's founding date or builder - antiquity claims (verify).

name: Pallippurathukavu Bhagavathi Temple
town_description: Kottayam is a major town in south-central Kerala, set amid rubber plantations and backwaters near the Meenachil River. Known as the 'City of Letters', it is a historic centre of Malayalam printing, publishing and education. The town is well connected by rail and road to Kochi and the rest of Kerala.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport, about 85 km northwest (verify)
travel.railway: Kottayam railway station, about 2-3 km away; temple is ~1 km south of the town
travel.road: On the Kollam-Theni highway corridor at Kodimatha/Chandakadavu, easily reached by local bus or auto from Kottayam town

visitor_information.best_time: September to February; festival season in Medam (April-May) for the Kumbhakuta Mahotsavam
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approximately 7:00 AM - 9:00 PM (verify - single tourism source)
